medications.purpose: Control blood pressure as first‑line therapy for hypertension in metabolic syndrome
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 recommends ACE‑I as first‑line antihypertensive for metabolic syndrome

medications.dose: 20 mg orally once daily in the evening
medications.duration: Lifelong — review annually and after 3 months lipid panel
medications.purpose: Reduce LDL‑C/non‑HDL‑C and lower ASCVD risk
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG181/NG28 advise statin for patients with QRISK ≥10% or metabolic syndrome

medications.dose: 500 mg orally once daily with evening meal, titrate by 500 mg weekly to 500 mg twice daily as tolerated
medications.duration: Lifelong — review annually and after each dose change
medications.purpose: Improve insulin sensitivity and prevent progression to type 2 diabetes in pre‑diabetes with BMI ≥30 kg/m²
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG28 recommends metformin for high‑risk pre‑diabetes (BMI ≥30) after lifestyle measures

medications.dose: 25 mg orally once daily, increase to 50 mg after 1 week if tolerated
medications.duration: 12 weeks then review; continue if benefit outweighs risk
medications.nice_justification: NICE guidance for anxiety disorders recommends SSRI as first‑line pharmacotherapy

interactions_checked.interaction: Minor increase in statin exposure; monitor CK if myopathy symptoms develop
interactions_checked.action: No dose adjustment needed; routine monitoring

contraindications.reason: Risk of fluid retention and worsening hypertension/obesity; contraindicated in patients with heart failure risk
contraindications.alternative: Metformin (already prescribed) or DPP‑4 inhibitor if metformin unsuitable

contraindications.reason: Can worsen glucose tolerance and dyslipidaemia in metabolic syndrome
contraindications.alternative: Discontinue hydrochlorothiazide or switch to low‑dose chlorthalidone 12.5 mg if needed

contraindications.reason: NICE NG136 advises against using beta‑blockers as first‑line in metabolic syndrome due to adverse metabolic effects

contraindications.alternative: DPP‑4 inhibitor (e.g., sitagliptin) if renal function is severely reduced

Liver function tests not provided – obtain baseline LFTs before initiating atorvastatin
Lipid profile and QRISK score not available – assume QRISK ≥10% given risk factors; calculate once labs are obtained
Allergy history not documented – verify no statin or ACE‑I intolerance before prescribing
No current NSAID use documented – advise avoidance of chronic NSAIDs due to renal and BP effects
treatment_summary: The plan addresses metabolic syndrome by continuing lisinopril for hypertension, initiating atorvastatin for dyslipidaemia, starting metformin to prevent progression of pre‑diabetes, and treating severe anxiety with sertraline. Hydrochlorothiazide should be discontinued to avoid worsening glucose tolerance. Baseline labs (eGFR, LFTs, lipid panel, iron studies) are required before starting new agents, and monitoring of renal function, electrolytes, CK, and glycaemic parameters will follow NICE recommendations.
